issue_context.title: Frozen tier exclusion doesn't prevent the search API to return failures for missing shards in the frozen tier

review_comments:
We are potentially artificially limiting the coordinator tier rewrite to [only indices that have the time range configured](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/114990/files#diff-0ad1800461d83a801b07a1207f4395615a0e9b6b5aad9ded33bda88e0f784d47R56) (partially mounted indices). We don't have to have this limitation for the `_tier` coordination rewrite however, the current implementation is sufficient for skipping frozen (where all indices do indeed have the `@timestamp` and `event.ingested` ranges). 

In the interest of keeping this fix targeted and contained I believe it's a good compromise for now but curious what you think.
now that this is merged, do we want to do the follow-up to allow filtering on tier to work on all indices?
It seems redundant that we are returning both the tier and exposing the constant field type too. Can't we get the current tier from the artificial data tier field type?

I believe we need the `tier` as the `CoordinatorRewriteContext` doesn't know of `indexSettings` otherwise https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/114990/files/67f82e9aa742e223de4cd6a76d496ac66987130e#diff-45c9ed5af87237215a5a11f3d2549aa678272c2cbc898b866b43516ec992fab5R60
The index settings would be needed for us to parse the `_tier_preference` setting.

I'm not sure if it should ? Or if we should keep just passing the `tier` ? It _seems_ that passing the tier is a smaller change (easier to test too).
I was under the impression that that is the same value that the constant field type that the context exposes returns, or is that something else?

The field type does not store any state but every time it evaluates it reaches out to the index settings for the `_tier_preference` value https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/114990/files/67f82e9aa742e223de4cd6a76d496ac66987130e#diff-e776fbfb85ffa7c76ad9fbbd1263953047589070bf15add46298deaf929778dbR95

The `QueryWriteContext` stores the index settings (but the `CoordinatorRewriteContext` doesn't)

I find it surprising that how we read the index setting here differs from how we read it above in CoordinatorRewriteContextProvider. Why is that? Reading the tier from index settings should require the same logic in those two places?

We've had performance issues in the past with parsing the tier preference from the settings. We now have a version of the `IndexMetadata` that does the parsing and caches the result for the lifetime of the `IndexMetadata`. 
Since the `CoordinatorRewriteContextProvider` has access to the `IndexMetadata` I preferred to take this route rather than re-parsing the setting.
perhaps make it super clear that the range info will only have a value for read only indices, because those are the only indices for which that info is populated in the cluster state

I believe read-only indices is a superset of where we actually have this optimization available - i.e. only for fully and partially mounted indices ?
I believe the comment is accurate if my assumption is correct (i.e. hot/warm indices don't have this optimization, cold/frozen ones - fully/partially mounted ones - do) but happy to clarify further if you have a better suggestion?
